content.user_title: Create and Review Short GIF Films
content.value_statement: Short animated films need consistent characters, deliberate cuts, and controlled generation costs. This skill guides shot planning, continuity review, selective retakes, and MP4 assembly through the public GIF Cinema CLI.
actual_capabilities: Plan short shot sequences with first and last poses, camera placement, subject scale, and motion direction.
Guide public CLI setup and run a synthetic offline smoke test for inspection, endpoint extraction, continuity reporting, and assembly.
Dry-run film scripts and assemble existing GIFs into an MP4 with a zero API-call cap.
Guide authorized shot generation with explicit API-call caps, disabled initial retries, and local still-image references.
Prepare selective retakes while preserving older outputs and reusing unchanged neighboring shots.
Review both cuts around replacements and report native frame counts, export FPS, visual faults, and estimated costs.
limitations: Requires a separately installed public runtime, Python 3.10+, Git, Pillow, FFmpeg, and ffprobe for script execution.
New generation requires user billing, an OpenAI API key, and supported model access; access is not guaranteed.
Shots support 2 to 16 frames; the public runtime lacks private smoothing, generated sound, automatic take ranking, and graphical undo.
The evaluation license permits personal non-commercial evaluation and research; commercial use, redistribution, and hosting require permission.

use_cases.title: Prototype a short animated story
use_cases.description: Plan a three-shot sequence, generate authorized candidates, and review character continuity before assembling a silent film.

use_cases.title: Assemble existing GIF studies
use_cases.description: Combine approved GIFs into an MP4 after a dry-run, with no generation calls and unchanged source files.

use_cases.title: Evaluate the public CLI offline
use_cases.description: Use synthetic media to check inspection, endpoints, continuity reporting, decoding, and zero-call rendering when ffprobe is available.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a three-shot story
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a three-shot silent film about [subject] performing [action]. Describe camera, first pose, last pose, and motion direction without making API calls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: develop a shot plan before installing or generating anything.

prompt_templates.title: Assemble existing GIFs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my GIFs in [directory] to prepare and dry-run a source-only film script. Assemble into [new output directory] with zero API calls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: export existing media without generation charges.

prompt_templates.title: Generate with reviewed references
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare shots for [story] using [identity reference]. Dry-run first and await approval of the call cap before generation. Disable retries and review each endpoint.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: maintain identity and composition across separately generated shots.

prompt_templates.title: Replace one shot selectively
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise only [shot ID] in [generating script] using [render directory]. Dry-run and request a call cap before execution. Preserve prior outputs and review both cuts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: evaluate a selective retake before updating the final montage.

output_examples.input: Plan a silent three-shot film where an astronaut receives a distant reply.
output: Shot 1: The astronaut raises one hand from a resting pose. Keep the horizon and subject scale stable.
Shot 2: A distant light answers while the astronaut holds the greeting pose. Review the first cut for pose continuity.
Shot 3: The astronaut acknowledges the light. Check identity, lighting, and motion direction across the second cut.

output_examples.input: Explain the expected export from the bundled astronaut example without generating new shots.
output_examples.output: The documented example assembles three existing 16-frame GIFs into a 7.68-second silent MP4 with zero generation calls. Playback still requires visual review.

output_examples.input: Outline a retake review for the middle shot without executing it.
output: Retain the original generating script and render directory. Revise only the middle shot and dry-run the updated script.
Request approval for the call cap and disable retries before execution.
Compare both neighboring cuts for identity, pose, scale, lighting, and action direction before updating the final montage.

best_practices: Dry-run every film script and agree on an explicit API-call cap before paid generation.
Review each endpoint and both neighboring cuts; decoding success and pixel metrics do not establish visual quality.
Keep original scripts and outputs for rollback, and exclude keys, private prompts, and unreviewed artifacts from public deliverables.
anti_patterns: Retrying uncertain or failed paid requests without reviewing delivery status and obtaining approval.
Using missing future references or expecting a middle-shot retake to regenerate neighboring shots automatically.
Treating higher export FPS as new motion or expecting private Studio smoothing and sound from the public runtime.

faq.question: Can I use the skill without an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Offline checks, dry-runs, and assembly of existing GIFs can run without a key. Use a zero API-call cap for source-only execution.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: Install the pinned public runtime with Python 3.10+, Git, Pillow, and FFmpeg. Script execution also requires ffprobe.

faq.question: Does this include the private Studio editor?
faq.answer: No. The public runtime excludes the private editor, RIFE smoothing, automatic last-frame dependency graph, and generated sound.

faq.question: How do references support continuity?
faq.answer: Use reviewed endpoint frames and identity references as local PNG, JPEG, or WebP files. Explicit references work through render, not simple generate.

faq.question: How are paid calls controlled?
faq.answer: Dry-run first, agree on a call cap, and start with retries disabled. Account and model support are checked through the actual request.

faq.question: Is commercial use permitted?
faq.answer: The evaluation license permits personal non-commercial evaluation and research. Commercial use, redistribution, and hosting require prior permission.
